title: PWA: delete blocks (and containers)
notes: Add first-class delete UI on the pipeline canvas (button per block + optional keyboard shortcut). Deleting a container should reparent its children sensibly (configurable: splice children up, or delete subtree). Must keep formatted pipeline script as canonical: update AST then re-render script.
acceptance: Canvas shows a Delete control for each block (STEP/ROUND/LOOP/FOREACH_TASK).
Deleting a STEP removes it and updates AST+script deterministically.
Deleting a container splices its children into the parent (no orphan nodes) and updates AST+script.
If deleting would produce an empty required container, insert a safe default child STEP.
All new UI strings are localized for en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ko, vi, ar, fr, es, ru, de.
No server start required; JS syntax check and a small AST transform test (unit-style) pass.

title: Pipeline: FOREACH_ACTION parse+render
notes: Extend the pipeline-script language + AST to support `FOREACH_ACTION` (nested under FOREACH_TASK). Ensure round-trip stability: script -> AST -> script preserves semantics and formatting rules (indentation, container children).
acceptance: Parser accepts `FOREACH_ACTION` as a container block with indented children.
Renderer outputs `FOREACH_ACTION` with correct indentation and children ordering.
Round-trip test fixtures cover nesting: ROUND -> FOREACH_TASK -> FOREACH_ACTION -> STEP <action_id>.
Backend stores updated AST alongside canonical script without breaking existing scripts.
No TCP binds; minimal python/js checks or unit tests pass.

title: Action Library: minimal API + copy-on-edit
notes: Introduce Action Library storage under runtime (e.g., `runtime/actions/`) with immutable default templates and user-defined actions. Provide minimal backend APIs to list/get actions and to create a user copy when editing a default action (copy-on-edit), returning a new `action_id` that pipeline blocks can reference.
acceptance: Runtime contains a clear actions layout: defaults vs user actions (gitignored runtime; no secrets).
API: list actions (with metadata: id, name, origin=default|user, inputs/outputs schema placeholder).
API: get action by id returns full template (tool binding + prompt/script fields).
API: edit default action does not mutate it; creates a new user action and returns new id (copy-on-edit).
PWA can switch a STEP block from one `action_id` to another (wiring only; no execution).
Any new user-facing strings localized across all required UI languages.

title: Runner: ActionResult state + explicit var passing (stub)
notes: Add a structured `ActionResult` record emitted per STEP execution (even if execution is stubbed). Persist it in runner state and make the next STEP receive prior outputs explicitly via a variable map, not by scanning folders. Keep scope tight: implement schema + persistence + plumbing without full tool execution.
acceptance: Define `ActionResult` schema: action_id, inputs, outputs, artifacts[], timestamps, status.
Runner writes ActionResult to `runtime/state/` and links it to cursor/ast_path.
Next step receives an explicit `vars` map derived from previous outputs (documented fields).
Resumability: restart does not duplicate already-committed ActionResults.
No TCP binds; python import/compile checks and a small unit-style runner test pass.

title: Task batches: details API + activate batch
notes: Build on the existing batches index by adding a batch-details endpoint and an explicit activation flow (select a batch to become the current task list for FOREACH_TASK). Add a minimal PWA interaction in the Task Batches panel to view/activate.
acceptance: Backend: GET batch details returns manifest + task_count + a bounded preview/tail of `tasks.jsonl`.
Backend: POST activate batch sets current tasks pointer for the active project (persisted under runtime/project state).
PWA: Task Batches panel can open details and activate a selected batch with clear status feedback.
WS broadcasts an event on activation so other clients refresh.
All new UI strings localized for all required languages.
No TCP binds; python/js checks pass.

title: Project settings: novel language (separate from UI)
notes: Add persisted per-project novel-writing settings with at least `novel_language`, distinct from UI locale. Provide minimal backend endpoints and a small PWA settings UI. Store under standardized runtime project layout, not in git.
acceptance: Backend exposes get/set project settings (includes novel_language).
PWA shows a novel language selector separate from UI language selector (no coupling).
Setting persists across reloads via runtime project state.
Default is sensible (e.g., inherit from UI only on first project creation, then independent).
All new user-facing strings localized across all required UI languages.
No TCP binds; JS syntax check and python compile/import checks pass.
